prompts: Create ONE full-bleed widescreen 16:9 high-definition hand-painted environment background for MGS Codec Simulator CQC, a 2D fighting-game stage. Use the supplied screenshots as direct visual evidence of the actual Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops (2006 PSP) location. Recompose the scene for a lateral fighting camera at human waist height, with a continuous flat unobstructed horizontal fighting lane across the bottom 20 percent. Preserve the game's concrete/steel/wood materials, subdued green-olive palette, proportions and period atmosphere. The references may be storyboard grids: synthesize only the specified environment into ONE continuous scene, never reproduce the grid. Remove all players, NPCs, UI bars, radar, text, subtitles, objective markers and logos. No people, no characters, no combat effects, no watermarks, no frame. Opaque finished environment, not a cutout. Subject: the actual RAIL BRIDGE in San Hieronymo, viewed ON THE BRIDGE DECK, not merely the nearby guardhouse. In reference1 the bottom row of all three frames shows the bridge; in reference2 the TOP MIDDLE frame shows it clearly. Preserve the long narrow metal truss structure: weathered dark reddish-brown steel diagonal braces forming repeated triangular/X spans, tall upright posts, open cross-bracing above, heavy weathered timber/plank safety barriers along both edges of the deck, gravel/earth-toned worn deck with TWO embedded parallel iron rails, muted yellow-green pools of utilitarian light, dark forested rocky gorge environment beyond the open truss. Translate the original axial camera into a side-dominant oblique lateral arena view: the deck and rails run mostly horizontally left to right, with the repeated truss on the far side as a strong background rhythm and enough perspective to reveal it is a spanning bridge. Keep the playable foreground deck broad and clear, no foreground truss blocking fighters. One stationary olive 1970s canvas military cargo truck may sit far back at the right end, consistent with reference1, small enough to leave the foreground open. Background is a dark olive rock-and-forest gorge, not a modern city; no invented towers, suspension cables, monumental arches, high-speed train or futuristic equipment. Emphasize the original bridge geometry and restrained PSP mood translated into polished 2D painted detail. No readable signs or extra props.

prompts: Create ONE full-bleed widescreen 16:9 high-definition hand-painted environment background for MGS Codec Simulator CQC, a 2D fighting-game stage. Use the supplied screenshots as direct visual evidence of the actual Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops (2006 PSP) location. Recompose the scene for a lateral fighting camera at human waist height, with a continuous flat unobstructed horizontal fighting lane across the bottom 20 percent. Preserve the game's concrete/steel/wood materials, subdued green-olive palette, proportions and period atmosphere. The references may be storyboard grids: synthesize only the specified environment into ONE continuous scene, never reproduce the grid. Remove all players, NPCs, UI bars, radar, text, subtitles, objective markers and logos. No people, no characters, no combat effects, no watermarks, no frame. Opaque finished environment, not a cutout. Subject: the RESEARCH LAB interior control-equipment room in San Hieronymo, specifically the gray institutional room from the first reference's MIDDLE and BOTTOM rows. This is the machine room visited in the Research Lab diversion mission, not a hospital bed ward. Preserve light gray slightly stained upper plaster walls, broad dark charcoal-gray lower wall dado, square dull gray-green floor tiles with pale grout, simple dull gray steel doors with small metal handles and lower ventilation slots, rectangular interior windows covered by closed white horizontal Venetian blinds, small old paper notice pinned on the wall with NO legible words. Against the back-left wall put the distinctive tall rectangular 1970s control/computer apparatus visible in the first reference BOTTOM LEFT frame: stacked olive/gray metal modules, several small black CRT rectangular displays, a few pale analog gauges and rows of tiny switches, dark equipment rack sections beneath, boxy utilitarian proportions. No modern flatscreens or holograms. A doorway at left connects to the narrow corridor shown in reference2; closed blinded windows run across the rear wall and right-side wall, and a plain metal door at the right matches reference3. Recompose into one modest rectangular side-on room with plenty of clear tiled foreground floor, low cold greenish fluorescent light and soft institutional shadows. Restrained detail drawn from the actual room; no laboratory glassware, invented glowing tanks, hospital beds, operating tables or sci-fi machinery. Do not reproduce the red game objective rings on the equipment, the players or HUD. The computer apparatus and blinds provide the identity of this Research Lab sector.
